key_insight: Jellyfish feeding efficiency is predicted to peak at the transition from Stokes pumping to inertial prey transport, where self-generated vortex rings enhance prey capture.
engineering_relevance: The findings could guide bioinspired underwater pumps and robots that use pulsating surfaces to transport particles efficiently.
method: Study prey capture relative to the energy spent deforming the body surface.
Develop a feeding-efficiency landscape spanning Stokes pumping and inertial transport.
Compare predictions with reported jellyfish sizes and beat frequencies and observe flows around moon jellyfish.
evidence_signal: Predictions explain reported sizes and beat frequencies across jellyfish taxa, while experiments on Aurelia aurita support vortex-ring-dominated transport.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative efficiency gains or validation range, limiting direct engineering design guidance.
paper_title: Vortex rings shape the feeding-efficiency landscape of jellyfish
